title: Target-Independent Micro-Interventions for Predicting Training Response Across Language-Model Families
abstract: arXiv:2609.08618v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Benchmark scores describe what a checkpoint can do now, but they do not determine how it will respond to the next training episode. We measure this missing state by branching four short, standardized, target-independent micro-interventions from the same checkpoint and recording their effects in a common capability space. Together with current capability, these responses form L-State; its pulse block supports a flexible direct readout and a structure-preserving operator readout. Under smooth local dynamics, the operator construction admits an end-to-end cross-family bound with explicit source- and target-family coordinate heterogeneity. In three-family leave-one-family-out development, both pulse readouts reduce source-standardized MSE by 39.4% relative to capability alone, while separating the best response and direction estimates. translated_title: 面向跨语言模型家族训练响应预测的目标无关微干预方法
translated_abstract: 基准测试分数描述了模型检查点当前能做什么，但并不能决定它将如何响应下一次训练。我们通过从同一检查点分支出四个简短、标准化、目标无关的微干预，并在一个共同的能力空间中记录它们的效果，来测量这一缺失的状态。这些响应与当前能力一起构成了 L-State；其脉冲块支持灵活的直接读出和保持结构的算子读出两种方式。在平滑局部动力学假设下，该算子构造允许建立端到端的跨家族理论界，并显式刻画源家族与目标家族的坐标异质性。在三个家族的留一家族交叉开发实验中，两种脉冲读出方式相比仅使用能力特征将源标准化 MSE 降低了 39.4%，同时将最佳响应估计与方向估计分离开来。在密封的 GLM-4-9B 模型上，直接读出和算子读出分别将 MSE 降低了 71.8% 和 78.3%。
tldr: 该论文提出通过四个目标无关的微干预构建 L-State 状态表示，能够跨不同语言模型家族预测模型对未来训练的响应，在 GLM-4-9B 上将预测误差（MSE）降低高达 78.3%。
